definition.name: Project Scaffolding / Code Generator
definition.name_zh: 项目脚手架 / 代码生成器
definition.overview:
A **Project Scaffolding / Code Generator** is a developer-facing creation tool that produces the starting point of a new software project: it holds a reusable starting-point definition — a template or generator program encoding a project's initial files, configuration, and boilerplate — collects a few inputs from the user, and emits a concrete, coherent starting codebase that the developer then owns and continues to build with their normal tools.

The defining structure is small:

```text
Reusable starting-point definition (template or generator)
└── Parameterized generation (user inputs shape the output)
    └── Emission of a starting project (files/directories the developer owns)
```

Everything else commonly associated with the category — public template registries, post-generation hooks, sub-generators, web-form workflows, publishing to git hosts, task history and audit — is widespread in mature products but not part of the defining core. The act is fundamentally a **one-time creation of a new project** (or of a new piece added to an existing one), not continuous maintenance, building, or transformation of existing code.
definition.overview_zh:
一个 **项目脚手架 / 代码生成器** 是一种面向开发者的创作工具，它生成新软件项目的起点：它持有一个可复用的起点定义——一个编码了项目初始文件、配置和样板代码的模板或生成器程序——从用户那里收集少量输入，然后输出一个具体、连贯的起始代码库，开发者随后拥有该代码库并继续使用其常规工具进行构建。

其定义结构很简单：

```text
可复用的起点定义（模板或生成器）
└── 参数化生成（用户输入塑造输出）
    └── 输出一个起始项目（开发者拥有的文件/目录）
```

通常与此类别相关的其他所有内容——公共模板注册中心、生成后钩子、子生成器、网页表单工作流、发布到 git 主机、任务历史和审计——在成熟产品中很常见，但并非定义核心的一部分。该操作本质上是 **一次性创建新项目**（或为现有项目添加新部分），而不是对现有代码的持续维护、构建或转换。
definition.dc:
Three properties. If any one is removed, the product is no longer recognizable as this Type:

- **A reusable starting-point definition** — a template or generator that encodes a project's starting structure: source files, configuration, manifests, docs, and tooling wiring. It exists as a first-class artifact held separately from any generated result, so it can be reused across many projects and improved over time. Without it, there is only ad-hoc copying of someone's repository.
- **Parameterized generation** — the user supplies inputs (project name, options, choices) that are resolved into the output; the same definition yields different projects. Without this, it is a static file copy or a sample repo.
- **Emission of a starting project** — the act writes a concrete starting codebase to disk (or, in enterprise variants, creates it in a remote system). The output is source code the developer takes ownership of and continues to develop with their own editor, build tools, and version control. Without this, it is a preview tool or a hosted app builder.

The binding across all three is *software-project creation semantics*: the output is a codebase, not a running hosted application and not a document.
definition.dc_zh:
三个属性。如果移除任何一个，产品将不再被视为此类型：

- **可复用的起始点定义** — 一个模板或生成器，编码项目的起始结构：源文件、配置、清单、文档和工具接线。它作为一等工件独立于任何生成结果存在，因此可以在多个项目中重复使用并随时间改进。没有它，就只能临时复制别人的仓库。
- **参数化生成** — 用户提供输入（项目名称、选项、选择），这些输入被解析为输出；相同的定义产生不同的项目。没有这个，它就是静态文件复制或示例仓库。
- **输出一个起始项目** — 该动作将具体的起始代码库写入磁盘（或者，在企业变体中，在远程系统中创建它）。输出是开发者拥有并继续使用自己的编辑器、构建工具和版本控制开发的源代码。没有这个，它就是预览工具或托管应用构建器。
所有三个的关联是*软件项目创建语义*：输出是一个代码库，而不是一个运行的托管应用程序，也不是文档。
definition.rules:
### The output leaves the application

The generated project is not managed inside the tool afterwards. Once emitted, it belongs to the developer's repository and evolves through normal development. This is the structural contrast with hosted app builders, where the application remains the runtime home of what was created.

### One-time creation, not continuous transformation

The defining act creates a new project (or a new piece). Products do not treat substantial existing code as their object of record; tools that rewrite or migrate existing codebases belong to a different Type.

### Parameters shape the output deterministically

Given the same template and the same inputs, the output is reproducible. This determinism — a versioned starting-point definition applied to explicit inputs — is what separates the Type from open-ended conversational code generation.

### Conflicts are guarded

Generation into a non-empty directory or over existing files is typically refused or explicitly warned about, protecting the developer's existing work.

### The template is the standard

In organizations, the maintained template functions as an enforceable starting convention: what every new project contains is decided by the template's author, not by each developer.
definition.rules_zh:
### 输出离开应用程序

生成的项目之后不在工具内管理。一旦输出，它就属于开发者的代码库，并通过正常开发演进。这是与托管应用构建器的结构性对比，后者应用程序仍然是所创建内容的运行时所在。

### 一次性创建，而非持续转换

定义操作创建一个新项目（或一个新部分）。产品不将大量现有代码视为其记录对象；重写或迁移现有代码库的工具属于不同类型。

### 参数确定性地塑造输出

给定相同的模板和相同的输入，输出是可复现的。这种确定性——将带版本的起点定义应用于显式输入——将此类型与开放式对话式代码生成区分开来。

### 冲突受到保护

生成到非空目录或覆盖现有文件通常会被拒绝或明确警告，以保护开发者的现有工作。

### 模板即标准

在组织中，维护的模板起到可强制执行的起始约定的作用：每个新项目包含什么是由模板作者决定的，而不是由每个开发者决定的。

definition.name: SQL Client
definition.overview:
A **SQL Client** is an interactive front-end that connects to a running SQL database system and lets the user work on it by writing and executing SQL, with results returned in inspectable form.

The defining structure is small:

```text
Connection to an external running SQL database system
└── SQL as the primary working interface (author → execute)
    └── Results returned in inspectable form (row sets + status/error feedback)
```

Everything else commonly associated with database tools — a graphical interface, a schema sidebar, saved connections, autocomplete, editable result grids, SSH tunnels — is widespread in current products but is not part of the defining core. The oldest and simplest form of the Type, the interactive terminal client, still satisfies the definition completely today.

A SQL Client holds no data of record. The data lives in the connected database server; the client is the surface through which a person converses with it in SQL.

When a product adds a schema catalog as its primary navigation, object/data development surfaces, and a persistent script workspace, it becomes a Database IDE. When a product centers on operating the deployment itself (configuration, backups, lifecycle), it becomes a Database Management Console. The SQL Client is the query surface those products are built around.
definition.overview_zh:
一个 **SQL Client** 是一个交互式前端，它连接到一个正在运行的 SQL 数据库系统，允许用户通过编写和执行 SQL 来进行操作，并以可检查的形式返回结果。

其核心定义结构很简单：

```text
连接到一个外部的、正在运行的 SQL 数据库系统
└── SQL 作为主要工作接口（作者 → 执行）
    └── 结果以可检查的形式返回（行集 + 状态/错误反馈）
```

其他通常与数据库工具相关的一切功能——图形用户界面、模式侧边栏、保存的连接、自动完成、可编辑的结果网格、SSH 隧道——在现代产品中普遍存在，但并非其定义核心的一部分。该类型最古老、最简单的形式——交互式终端客户端——在今天仍然完全满足定义。

SQL Client 不持有任何记录数据。数据存储在连接的数据库服务器中；客户端只是人通过 SQL 与之对话的表面。

当一个产品添加一个模式目录作为其主要导航、对象/数据开发界面以及一个持久的脚本工作空间时，它就变成了一个 Database IDE。当一个产品以运维部署本身（配置、备份、生命周期）为中心时，它就变成了一个 Database Management Console。SQL Client 是这些产品构建所围绕的查询表面。
definition.dc:
```text
Connection to an external running SQL database system
└── SQL as the primary working interface (author → execute)
    └── Results returned in inspectable form (row sets + status/error feedback)
```

Three properties. If any one is removed, the product is no longer recognizable as a SQL Client:

- **Connection to an external running database system** — the client is a front-end; the database of record lives on the server it connects to. Without this, the product is a driver, a library, or a connection manager.
- **SQL as the primary working interface** — the user works by writing SQL statements and executing them against the connection, whether typed at a prompt, written in an editor, or supplied as a script file. Without this, the product is a point-and-click data browser, not an SQL client.
- **Results returned in inspectable form** — queries return row sets the user can read; every statement returns status and error feedback. Without this, execution is fire-and-forget — a batch runner, not a conversation.

The binding to SQL itself is part of the definition. Tools with the same shape over other engine classes — graph query languages, vector search, time-series, SPARQL — are different Application Types.
definition.dc_zh:
连接到外部运行的SQL数据库系统
└── SQL作为主要工作接口（编写 → 执行）
    └── 结果以可检查的形式返回（行集 + 状态/错误反馈）
definition.rules:
### The client holds no data of record

Everything the client shows — rows, schema, status — is read from the connected server at execution time. The client is a mirror and a messenger, not a store. Close the connection and the client retains only its own conveniences (saved connections, query history).

### Execution is authoritative and immediate

Statements execute on the server as they are submitted. A destructive statement is not made safe by the client; safety comes from postures the client offers (read-only modes, confirmation dialogs, error gates that stop a script at the first failure) and from the server's own permissions. This is why error feedback is a first-class part of the results surface, not an afterthought.

### The catalog view is a convenience, not the authority

What the sidebar or describe command shows is queried from the server. If the schema changes elsewhere, the client's view changes with the next refresh. The client never becomes the system of record for the schema.

### One conversation, one connection (terminal clients)

A terminal client session is bound to one connection at a time; switching means reconnecting. Graphical clients commonly hold several connections in parallel tabs. Both satisfy the Type; the difference is convenience, not structure.

### Scripts run as written

When a file of statements is executed, the client sends them in order and reports per-statement outcomes. Products differ in whether a failure stops the run, whether the whole file is wrapped in one transaction, and how errors are reported to the calling shell — but the invariant is that the script's SQL is executed as authored, with results and errors visible.
definition.rules_zh:
### 客户端不持有记录数据

客户端显示的所有内容——行、模式、状态——都是在执行时从连接的服务器读取的。客户端是一面镜子和一个信使，而不是一个存储。关闭连接后，客户端只保留其自身的便捷功能（保存的连接、查询历史记录）。

### 执行是权威且即时的

语句在提交时即在服务器上执行。破坏性语句不会因客户端而变得安全；安全性来自客户端提供的模式（只读模式、确认对话框、在第一个失败处停止脚本的机制）以及服务器自身的权限。这就是为什么错误反馈是结果表面的一个核心组成部分，而不是事后的想法。

### 目录视图是便捷的，而非权威的

侧边栏或描述命令显示的内容是从服务器查询的。如果模式在其他地方发生变化，客户端的视图将在下次刷新时随之改变。客户端永远不会成为模式的记录系统。

### 一次对话，一个连接（终端客户端）

一个终端客户端会话一次绑定到一个连接；切换意味着重新连接。图形客户端通常在并行选项卡中持有多个连接。两者都满足该类型；区别在于便捷性，而非结构。

### 脚本按原样运行

当执行一个包含语句的文件时，客户端按顺序发送它们并报告每个语句的结果。产品之间的不同之处在于失败是否停止运行、整个文件是否包装在一个事务中、以及如何向调用 shell 报告错误——但不变的是，脚本的 SQL 按原样执行，结果和错误都可见。

definition.name: Web Development IDE
definition.overview:
A **Web Development IDE** is a development environment specialized for building software that is delivered through a web browser — pages, sites, and applications written in web technologies: HTML, CSS, JavaScript/TypeScript, and the frameworks built on them.

Its defining core is small:

```text
Web-target working scope (project / site)
└── Web-stack-integrated editing
    └── The browser-terminated loop
        (build/serve → rendered preview in a browser → refresh on change)
```

Everything else commonly associated with web development tooling — integrated debugging, test runners, package managers, framework wizards, visual page editing, publishing machinery — is standard capability in mature products or a property of one of the category's two product families, not part of the definition.

The category has two long-standing product families: **code-first** environments, where the code is the substrate and the tooling is a full development environment bound to the web stack; and **visual/authoring-first** editors, where the rendered page is the primary surface and code is edited alongside it. Both work on standard web files; both close their loop in a browser.
definition.overview_zh:
一个**Web开发集成开发环境**是一种专为构建通过Web浏览器交付的软件而设计的开发环境——这些软件包括使用Web技术编写的页面、站点和应用程序：HTML、CSS、JavaScript/TypeScript，以及基于它们构建的框架。

其定义性核心很小：

```text
面向Web的工作范围（项目/站点）
└── Web技术栈集成编辑
    └── 浏览器终结的循环
        （构建/提供服务 → 在浏览器中渲染预览 → 更改时刷新）

所有其他通常与Web开发工具相关的东西——集成调试、测试运行器、包管理器、框架向导、可视化页面编辑、发布机制——在成熟产品中是标准功能，或属于该类别两大产品家族之一的特性，并非定义的一部分。

该类别有两个长期存在的产品家族：**代码优先**的环境，其中代码是基础，工具链是绑定到Web技术栈的完整开发环境；以及**视觉/创作优先**的编辑器，其中渲染后的页面是主要界面，代码在旁边编辑。两者都处理标准Web文件；两者都在浏览器中闭合其循环。
definition.dc:
```text
Web-target working scope (project / site)
└── Web-stack-integrated editing
    └── The browser-terminated loop
```

Three properties. If any one is removed, the product is no longer recognizable as a web development environment:

- **Web-target working scope** — a first-class working context whose subject is a web application or site: the unit to which tooling, preview, and settings attach. It may be a formal project, a plain folder opened as one, or a site definition. Without it, the tool is a file editor with no memory of what belongs together.
- **Web-stack-integrated editing** — editing assistance computed against web semantics: the structure of HTML documents (elements, nesting, attributes), CSS as rules with selectors and properties, and JavaScript/TypeScript symbols. Mature products carry this awareness *across* the languages — for example, completing CSS class names inside JavaScript code, or showing which style rules affect a selected element. Without it, the tool is a generic text editor.
- **The browser-terminated loop** — the environment operates the app's development cycle from within: it builds or bundles where needed (with its own tooling or by delegating to framework command-line tools), serves the app locally, presents the **rendered result in a browser surface** — a built-in preview pane or a launched browser — and refreshes it as changes are saved. The browser is the application's execution surface; the edit→see loop closes inside the environment. Without it, the developer edits code and separately operates a server and a browser — the working pattern of a plain code editor.
definition.dc_zh:
Web目标工作范围（项目/站点）
└── Web技术栈集成编辑
    └── 浏览器终止的循环
definition.rules:
### The browser is the execution surface

The environment never runs the web app itself. It builds, serves, renders, and attaches. This has two consequences: the preview is only as truthful as the serving setup, and debugging requires the environment to connect to the browser or Node runtime rather than control a process of its own.

### Editing assistance follows the stack's cross-language relationships

The web stack is multi-language by nature: markup, styles, and scripts reference each other (classes used in both CSS and JS, elements bound to rules). Mature environments compute assistance across those boundaries, not per file.

### Visual operations must write standard files (authoring family)

The authoring family's contract with its users is that visual editing produces ordinary HTML and CSS — no proprietary layer, no lock-in. Styling controls read and write real CSS rules; inline styling can be promoted into rules. This rule is the boundary against website builders.

### Debugging is family-dependent

A code-first web IDE integrates debugging against browser and Node runtimes. An authoring-first web editor typically does not integrate a debugger at all; execution inspection happens in the browser's developer tools. Both remain full members of the Type.

### Publish and deploy are separate from the loop

Finishing work means getting it onto a host. The authoring family treats publishing as a first-class step (site → host); the code-first family delegates it to framework and platform tooling. Neither is part of the defining loop.
definition.rules_zh:
### 浏览器是执行表面

该环境从不运行Web应用本身。它进行构建、提供服务、渲染和连接。这有两个后果：预览的真实性取决于服务设置，调试需要环境连接到浏览器或Node运行时，而不是控制自身的进程。

### 编辑辅助遵循技术栈的跨语言关系

Web技术栈本质上是多语言的：标记、样式和脚本相互引用（CSS和JS中都使用的类，与规则绑定的元素）。成熟的环境在这些边界上计算辅助，而不是按文件进行。

### 可视化操作必须写入标准文件（创作家族）

创作家族与其用户的契约是，可视化编辑产生普通的HTML和CSS——没有专有层，没有锁定。样式控件读写真实的CSS规则；内联样式可以被提升为规则。此规则是与网站构建器的边界。

### 调试依赖于家族

代码优先的Web IDE集成了针对浏览器和Node运行时的调试。创作优先的Web编辑器通常根本不集成调试器；执行检查发生在浏览器的开发者工具中。两者仍然是该类型的完整成员。

### 发布和部署独立于循环

完成工作意味着将其放到主机上。创作家族将发布视为一等步骤（站点 → 主机）；代码优先家族将其委托给框架和平台工具。两者都不属于定义性循环。

definition.name: Browser Compatibility Testing Platform
definition.name_zh: 浏览器兼容性测试平台
aliases_zh: 浏览器兼容性测试工具
definition.overview:
A **Browser Compatibility Testing Platform** gives a web team on-demand access to a large, selectable catalog of browser environments — browsers and specific versions running on operating systems (and, in many products, real devices and screen resolutions) that the team could not practically assemble on its own — and runs the team's own web application inside whichever environment is chosen. The tester observes what happens, either by driving the remote browser interactively, by executing existing test scripts against a hosted browser grid, or by capturing screenshots in bulk across many configurations at once.

The problem it solves is structural: a web application must work on combinations of browser, browser version, and operating system that no individual machine can host. An old browser may not install on a modern operating system; a Safari version may exist only on macOS; yesterday's browser release and a five-year-old browser must both be checked before release. The platform maintains that environment matrix as a service, so verifying compatibility becomes a matter of selecting an environment and pointing it at a URL rather than maintaining a room full of machines.

The boundary of the Type: the platform's own artifact is **the environment and the observable session** — not the test cases (they belong to the team, or to test-management products), not ongoing operational vigilance (that is monitoring), and not consumer browsing (that is a web browser).
definition.overview_zh:
一个**浏览器兼容性测试平台**为网络团队提供按需访问一个大型、可选的浏览器环境目录的能力——包括运行在操作系统上的浏览器及特定版本（在许多产品中，还包括真实设备和屏幕分辨率），这些环境是团队自身难以实际组织的——并在所选环境中运行团队自己的 Web 应用程序。测试员通过交互式驱动远程浏览器、针对托管的浏览器网格执行现有测试脚本，或一次性跨多种配置批量截取屏幕截图来观察发生的情况。

它解决的问题是结构性的：Web 应用程序必须在浏览器、浏览器版本和操作系统的多种组合上运行，而任何单台机器都无法承载所有组合。一个旧版浏览器可能无法在现代操作系统上安装；某个 Safari 版本可能只存在于 macOS 上；昨天的浏览器版本和五年前的浏览器都必须在发布前进行检查。该平台将该环境矩阵作为一种服务进行维护，因此验证兼容性就变成了选择一个环境并将其指向 URL 的问题，而不是维护一整间机房的机器。

类型的边界：平台自身的产出物是**环境和可观察的会话**——而不是测试用例（它们属于团队或测试管理产品），也不是持续的运营监控（那是监控），更不是消费者浏览（那是 Web 浏览器）。
definition.dc: An **environment** is one selectable combination in the platform's catalog: a browser type and version running on an operating system, commonly extended with device model and screen resolution. The catalog deliberately spans versions and operating systems the team cannot run locally — legacy browsers kept available long after their end of life, pre-release (beta/developer) channels of upcoming versions, and operating systems the team does not use. This catalog is the platform's backbone: every workflow begins by choosing from it, and its breadth is the compatibility dimension itself. In mature products the catalog is large and explicitly enumerated, with each combination linked to both a manual and an automated way to run against it.
definition.dc_zh: 一个**环境**是平台目录中的一个可选组合：一个浏览器类型和版本运行在操作系统上，通常扩展以设备型号和屏幕分辨率。该目录故意涵盖了团队无法在本地运行的版本和操作系统——生命周期结束后仍长期可用的旧版浏览器、即将版本的预发布（测试版/开发者）渠道，以及团队不使用的操作系统。该目录是平台的支柱：每个工作流都始于从中选择，其广度本身就是兼容性维度。在成熟产品中，目录庞大且明确枚举，每个组合都链接到手动和自动两种运行方式。
definition.rules:
- **The environment is executed exactly as selected.** A run or session pinned to a specific browser version runs in that version — this pinning is the point; "latest" is just one selectable value among many, and pre-release channels are selectable too.
- **Concurrency is the scarce resource.** Plans commonly bound how many sessions/runs execute at once; large matrix runs are sized against that limit, and parallel execution is the platform's unit of scale.
- **Sessions are ephemeral and cleaned.** Hosted environments are provisioned for the task and released afterward; vendors commonly state that session data is wiped so successive customers never share residue. Testing state must live in the target application or test code, not in the environment.
- **Private targets require the tunnel.** The platform can only see what it can reach; localhost and firewalled staging are invisible until a connector relays them. Conversely, anything reachable through the tunnel is testable by every mode.
- **Automated statuses must be reported back.** The platform records what the test framework emits; pass/fail per environment typically arrives through the framework's integration or an API call. Result matrices and badges reflect reported state, not the platform's own judgment of the page.
- **The catalog is maintained, not static.** New browser and OS releases appear (often including beta channels), and very old environments are eventually retired; a team's support matrix therefore needs occasional re-validation against the current catalog.
- **Legacy environments exist precisely because local installation is impractical** — that is the platform's core value, not a niche feature. Testing an end-of-life browser is one of the most common reasons to open the product.
definition.rules_zh:
- **环境将完全按照所选方式执行。** 固定到特定浏览器版本的运行或会话将在该版本中运行——这种固定正是关键所在；“最新版”只是众多可选值中的一个，预发布渠道也是可选的。
- **并发是稀缺资源。** 计划通常限制同时执行的会话/运行数量；大规模矩阵运行会针对此限制进行评估，而并行执行是平台的扩展单位。
- **会话是临时性的并会被清理。** 托管环境为任务而配置并在任务完成后释放；供应商通常声明会话数据会被清除，因此后续客户永远不会共享残留物。测试状态必须存在于目标应用程序或测试代码中，而不是环境中。
- **私有目标需要隧道。** 平台只能看到它能触及的内容；localhost 和防火墙后的预发布环境在连接器中继它们之前是不可见的。相反，任何通过隧道可达的目标都可以通过所有模式进行测试。
- **自动化状态必须被报告回平台。** 平台记录测试框架发出的内容；每个环境的通过/失败状态通常通过框架的集成或 API 调用到达。结果矩阵和徽章反映的是报告的状态，而不是平台自己对页面的判断。
- **目录是维护的，而不是静态的。** 新的浏览器和操作系统版本会发布（通常包括 beta 渠道），非常古老的环境最终会被淘汰；因此团队的支持矩阵需要偶尔根据当前目录进行重新验证。
- **遗留环境之所以存在，恰恰是因为本地安装不切实际**——这是平台的核心价值，而不是一个细分功能。测试一个生命周期结束的浏览器是打开该产品最常见的原因之一。

definition.name: Code Quality Platform
definition.overview:
A **Code Quality Platform** is the system of record for the health of a codebase. It continuously analyzes a project's source code, keeps the resulting findings and measurements as persistent platform-side state over time, holds a configurable definition of what "good code" means for that project, and reports a pass/fail verdict on every change into the team's merge and release workflow.

Its reason to exist is a structural gap: code analyzers (linters, bug detectors, complexity and duplication tools) produce findings for a single run, but nothing that runs once can answer "is this codebase getting better or worse?" or "may this change be merged?". The platform sits between the analysis engines and the delivery workflow: it accumulates analysis results into a durable quality picture — issues, metrics, ratings, trends — and turns them into a go/no-go signal attached to each pull request and branch.

The defining core is deliberately small:

```text
Managed project (bound to a repository)
└── Recorded analysis runs (on onboarding and on every change)
    └── Persistent quality state (issues + metrics + history)
        └── Configurable quality standard (rules and/or thresholds)
            └── Quality verdict surfaced in the delivery workflow
```

Everything else commonly associated with these products — coverage tracking, letter grades, pull-request comments, portfolios, self-hosted servers, AI fix suggestions — is standard market capability or optional, not part of the definition.
definition.overview_zh:
一个 **代码质量平台** 是代码库健康状态的记录系统。它持续分析项目的源代码，将产生的发现和测量结果作为平台端持久化状态保存一段时间，并持有该项目“良好代码”的可配置定义，然后在每次变更进入团队的合并和发布工作流时报告通过/失败的判定结果。

其存在的理由源于一个结构性缺口：代码分析器（静态检查工具、错误检测工具、复杂度和重复度工具）只能为单次运行产生发现结果，但任何一次性的运行都无法回答“这个代码库是在变好还是变坏？”或“这次变更是否可以合并？”。该平台位于分析引擎和交付工作流之间：它将分析结果累积成一个持久的质量全景图——问题、度量指标、评级、趋势——并将它们转化为附加在每个拉取请求和分支上的“放行/禁止”信号。

其核心定义是有意设计得非常精简：

```text
受管项目（绑定到代码仓库）
└── 记录的分析运行（在接入时和每次变更时执行）
    └── 持久的质量状态（问题 + 度量指标 + 历史记录）
        └── 可配置的质量标准（规则 和/或 阈值）
            └── 在交付工作流中呈现的质量判定结果
```

其他通常与这些产品相关的一切功能——覆盖率追踪、字母等级评定、拉取请求评论、项目组合视图、自托管服务器、AI修复建议——属于市场标准能力或可选功能，并非该定义的一部分。
definition.dc:
**Managed project.** The unit of management is a project bound to a source repository (or a defined part of one). Projects live inside an organization that usually mirrors the structure of the connected Git provider. Branches and pull requests of the project are first-class analysis subjects.

**Recorded analysis runs.** Each time code changes — and once when the project is first added — an analysis run executes (from the platform's own engines, from third-party analyzers the platform wraps, or both) and its results are recorded. The run, not the tool invocation, is the unit of history: platforms display a timeline of analyses and how measures evolved between them.

**Persistent quality state.** Findings and measurements are stored and maintained by the platform over time:

- **Issues** — individual findings bound to precise code locations, each raised because a rule was violated: bugs, code smells, complexity and duplication findings, security findings, lint results from wrapped tools.
- **Metrics** — measures computed for the project, branch, directory, or file: issue counts by severity, duplicated-code density, complexity, size (lines of code), test coverage, and remediation-effort estimates often expressed as technical debt.
- **History and trends** — the state survives across runs, which is what makes deterioration visible and improvement measurable.

**Configurable quality standard.** A maintained definition of "good" for this code, with two faces:

- a **rule set** — which checks apply (a per-language profile of rules, a pattern configuration, a set of enabled analyzers, or a committed configuration file in the repository);
- **thresholds and conditions** — what the measured values must satisfy for a change to be acceptable (no new high-severity issues, complexity below X, duplication below Y, coverage not decreased).

**Quality verdict.** The evaluation of an analysis run's results against the standard, reported as a visible pass/fail status attached to the change — a commit status, a pull-request check, or a gate badge — and used in merge/release decisions. Whether the verdict merely reports or actively blocks the merge is a wiring decision; the verdict itself is the invariant.
definition.dc_zh:
**托管项目。** 管理单元是绑定到源代码仓库（或其明确定义部分）的项目。项目存在于组织内，该组织通常反映所连接Git提供商的结构。项目的分支和拉取请求是一等分析主体。

**录制分析运行。** 每次代码变更时——以及项目首次添加时——平台会执行一次分析运行（来自平台自身的引擎、平台封装的第三方分析器，或两者兼有），并记录其结果。历史记录的单元是运行而非工具调用：平台展示分析时间线以及各度量指标在运行间的变化。

**持久质量状态。** 发现结果和测量值由平台随时间存储和维护：
- **问题** — 绑定到精确代码位置的单个发现，每条都因违反规则而产生：缺陷、代码异味、复杂度与重复代码发现、安全发现、封装工具的 lint 结果。
- **度量指标** — 为项目、分支、目录或文件计算的测量值：按严重级别统计的问题数、重复代码密度、复杂度、规模（代码行数）、测试覆盖率，以及通常以技术债务形式表示的修复工作量估算。
- **历史与趋势** — 状态在多次运行中持续存在，这使得质量恶化变得可见，改进得以衡量。

definition.rules:
- **The verdict is attached to the change, and enforcement is a choice.** The gate status always exists as a visible signal; whether it blocks merging or fails the pipeline depends on how the team wires the Git provider's branch protection and CI. Products document both postures; blocking is never forced by the platform alone.
- **Findings belong to code locations and persist until resolved.** An issue remains associated with its line(s) across analyses; when the code changes such that the finding disappears, it closes; dispositions (false positive, accepted) are remembered and reapplied on later runs rather than re-raised.
- **New-issue focus shapes what a review reports.** In the dominant modern mode, a pull-request analysis reports what the change introduced — not the pre-existing debt of untouched code. Pre-existing findings remain browsable in the platform. Consequence: a first analysis after onboarding may surface old-code findings that per-change reviews never showed.
- **Baselines gate the gate.** Before a baseline or a new-code definition exists, the verdict may be "not computed" rather than pass or fail.
- **The platform consumes coverage; it does not produce it.** Coverage conditions depend on the team uploading reports from their test tooling; missing reports are a first-class failure mode (gaps, stale data).
- **Organizational standards can override repository settings.** An org-level policy typically auto-applies to newly added repositories; removing it can restore the repository's previous settings. Built-in default policies are commonly protected from edit/delete.
- **The standard is code too, somewhere.** The rule set lives either platform-side (profiles/patterns edited in the console) or repository-side (committed configuration files), with committed files usually required to be on the default branch to take effect.
- **Assignment targets authors.** New findings are typically assigned to the committer/author of the offending line when the person can be matched to a platform user; reassignment is always possible.
definition.rules_zh:
- **判定结果附属于变更，执行与否取决于选择。** 门禁状态始终作为一个可见信号存在；它是否阻止合并或导致流水线失败，取决于团队如何配置 Git 提供商的分支保护规则和 CI。产品会记录这两种姿态；阻止操作永不会由平台单方面强制执行。
- **发现结果属于代码位置，并在解决前一直存在。** 一个问题在多次分析中都与其所在的代码行关联；当代码变更导致该发现消失时，它会被关闭；处置方式（误报、已接受）会被记住，并在后续运行中重新应用，而不是重新提出。
- **关注新问题的模式塑造了评审报告的内容。** 在主流的现代模式下，拉取请求分析报告的是该变更引入了什么——而不是未触及代码的既有技术债。既有的发现结果在平台中仍可浏览。结果是：接入后的首次分析可能会暴露之前每次变更评审都未显示的旧代码问题。
- **基线决定门禁的有效性。** 在存在基线或新代码定义之前，判定结果可能是“未计算”而非通过或失败。
- **平台使用覆盖率，但不产生覆盖率。** 覆盖率条件取决于团队上传其测试工具的报告；缺少报告是一种一级失败模式（数据缺口、过时数据）。
- **组织标准可以覆盖仓库设置。** 组织级策略通常会自动应用于新添加的仓库；移除该策略可以恢复仓库之前的设置。内置的默认策略通常受到保护，不可编辑/删除。
- **标准本身也是代码，位于某处。** 规则集要么存在于平台侧（在控制台编辑的配置文件/模式），要么存在于代码仓库侧（提交的配置文件），提交的配
